memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: While the Israelites were in the wilderness, a man was found gathering wood on the Sabbath day. Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses and Aaron and the whole assembly, and they kept him in custody, because it was not clear what should be done to him. Then the Lord said to Moses, "The man must die. The whole assembly must stone him outside the camp." So the assembly took him outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the Lord commanded Moses. — Num 15:32-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a hard passage, and we must not rush past its difficulty. A man is executed for gathering wood on the Sabbath. To modern ears it sounds shockingly severe, and we should be honest about how heavy it feels. But we need to understand it in its setting rather than either dismissing it or letting it distort our picture of God.

This was not really about firewood. It came immediately after the teaching on "defiant" sin — the high-handed rebellion just described. The man was not accidentally forgetting the Sabbath; he was openly, deliberately defying a command God had given at the very foundation of the covenant. The Sabbath was a sign of Israel's relationship with God, and to trample it defiantly was to reject Him publicly. This was a test case of the principle just laid down.

Under the old covenant, at this crucial moment of Israel's national formation, God's holiness was displayed in visible, immediate judgment. He was teaching a young nation that His word could not be treated with contempt. Sin is deadly serious — far more serious than we usually feel it to be.

We do not live under this civil law today; the Sabbath regulations were part of the old covenant, and Christians differ on how the Sabbath principle applies now. But the deeper truth stands: rebellion against God brings death. And here the gospel breaks in with staggering grace. We have all defied God and deserve judgment — yet Christ was taken "outside the camp" and put to death in our place. The sentence this man received is the sentence Jesus bore for us. What sobering justice; what astonishing mercy.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you take the seriousness of sin as heavily as God does here?
2. Why is it important to read this event in its covenant setting?
3. How does Christ dying "outside the camp" transform how you see this passage?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy Father, teach me to take sin seriously and never to treat Your word with contempt. Thank You that Christ was taken outside the camp and bore the judgment I deserved. Let me live in reverent gratitude for such mercy. Amen.
